title: Freelancer Bookkeeping Service Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Bookkeeping services and accounting software that compete for the same customers and jobs as Kees de Boekhouder, the Amsterdam bookkeeping-as-a-service company modeled in this domain (with its sister brand Founders for BV clients): Dutch freelancers and sole proprietors (eenmanszaak), starting entrepreneurs, VOF partnerships and small BVs who need receipts, invoices and bank transactions captured, the quarterly btw-aangifte and the yearly income tax return (or corporate tax return and annual accounts) filed with the Belastingdienst, and someone to ask about deductions, reservations and the Wet DBA. Kees de Boekhouder is included as the modeled company so that the other players' figures can be read against its own 10,000+ clients and roughly 100 staff.
inclusionLogic: bookkeeping-as-a-service propositions that bundle an administration app with a personal, named bookkeeper who carries the filing responsibility on a fixed monthly or yearly fee — the head-to-head alternative to Kees de Boekhouder for a freelancer who does not want to do the books alone

software-only zzp accounting packages in which the freelancer keeps the books, files the VAT return and increasingly the income tax return from the tool itself, optionally with an accountant added by the user — the 'do it yourself for a few euros a month' alternative that every Kees prospect compares against
SME accounting suites sold to small businesses and their accountants, which a growing VOF or BV client may adopt together with an external accountancy firm instead of staying with Kees or Founders
traditional local bookkeepers and administratiekantoren, the incumbent hourly or per-return service that Kees was founded to replace and that clients still switch from (modeled as one generic player)
notes: Business stats are only included when they were found on official company websites (home, pricing, about, plan and investor pages); each stat preserves the company's reported scope and period, and players for which no official figure could be verified carry only the figures that could be. Numbers that are only available from third-party listings or review aggregators are either left out or explicitly labeled as third-party in the scope field.

Vendors report at very different scopes: Moneybird and e-Boekhouden.nl publish cumulative 'entrepreneurs who have used the platform' counters, SnelStart reports current entrepreneurs and employees for the whole company, Jortt reports a zzp user count, MoneyMonk and Rompslomp publish review scores and counts, while Kees de Boekhouder reports active clients served by its own bookkeepers. None of these figures are directly comparable with each other or with Kees' 10,000+ entrepreneurs.

Prices are listed as published on the official pricing pages at the time of access, excluding VAT unless stated otherwise, and several vendors run promotional first-period prices (free months for starters, discounted first quarters) that are quoted with their conditions rather than normalized to a list price.

Several players sit inside larger groups: SnelStart and Rompslomp are part of Visma, Tellow (Shine Netherlands B.V.) is part of Ageras, and Founders Finance B.V. is the sister company of Kees de Boekhouder rather than a competitor; Founders is therefore folded into the modeled-company entry.

Exact Online is listed as the representative SME accounting suite with which a Kees client's external accountant may work; no product-level statistic could be verified on an official page within the research scope of this domain, so its entry carries no business stats.

players.name: Kees de Boekhouder (modeled company, with Founders)
players.description: Kees de Boekhouder is the modeled subject of this domain: an Amsterdam bookkeeping-as-a-service company founded in 2009 by Kees Monteban and Marlou ter Berg for freelancers who found existing solutions too complex and overpriced. It combines a proprietary web and mobile administration app (dashboard with quarterly revenue, costs, profit and VAT position, Scan & Herken receipt recognition, quotes and invoices, a Ponto PSD2 bank connection synchronising four times a day) with a personal, internally trained bookkeeper who checks the administration, files the quarterly VAT return, prepares the annual accounts and files the income tax return, all on a fixed yearly subscription invoiced monthly: eenmanszaak EUR 840, VOF EUR 1,140 for two partners plus EUR 100 per extra partner, and through the sister company Founders (Founders Finance B.V., founded 2018) holding BV EUR 1,750 and werkmaatschappij EUR 2,450 per year ex VAT. It serves more than 10,000 entrepreneurs from offices in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht with roughly 100 staff, of whom about 40 percent are bookkeepers, grows through partnerships with professional associations such as BNO, DuPho, Kunstenbond and Stichting BOK, and has been backed by Vortex Capital Partners since a buyout announced in May 2022. It is listed here so that the other players' scale can be read against it.

players.name: Tellow
players.description: Tellow (Shine Netherlands B.V., founded in Amsterdam in 2015 and now part of Ageras) is the closest head-to-head alternative to Kees de Boekhouder: a zzp accounting app with a free plan, paid self-service plans and a 'Compleet' plan that adds a personal bookkeeper who reviews the books and files the returns, combined with a business IBAN and cards that Kees explicitly does not offer. For a freelancer who wants software-first bookkeeping with the option of a human filing layer and banking in the same app, Tellow Compleet is the proposition a Kees prospect compares on price and on the depth of the personal relationship. Third-party listings put its user base at 50,000+ zzp'ers, a figure not verified on an official Tellow page and therefore not recorded as a business stat.

players.name: Moneybird
players.description: Moneybird is the best-known Dutch software-only accounting package for freelancers and small businesses: invoicing, receipts, bank feeds and VAT returns in a polished web and mobile app, sold in four self-service tiers from a few euros a month with a 60-day trial, plus an optional Moneybird business account. It has been around for roughly 17 years and claims more than 400,000 entrepreneurs. For a Kees prospect it is the 'do it yourself for EUR 15 to 41 a month' alternative: cheaper, but the freelancer keeps the books and the fiscal responsibility and has to add an accountant separately for the income tax return.

players.name: e-Boekhouden.nl
players.description: e-Boekhouden.nl, founded in 2002 and based in Brabant, is the volume player in Dutch online bookkeeping software: a low-priced ZZP package with invoicing, receipts, bank links and VAT returns, a Standaard package for small businesses and 15 months free for starters, backed by roughly 90 staff and a 4.5-star Trustpilot rating. Its claim that over 500,000 entrepreneurs have used the platform makes it, with Moneybird, the default self-service comparison for a starting entrepreneur who is deciding between software at EUR 5 to 24 a month and a personal bookkeeper at EUR 70 a month.

players.name: Jortt
players.description: Jortt (Almere, KvK 64073319) is the software-only package that goes furthest in replacing the bookkeeper: it holds its own PSD2 licence from De Nederlandsche Bank for bank connections, positions an AI 'boekhoudbot' that books transactions automatically, and builds the income tax (IB) and corporate tax (VPB) returns, payroll and Peppol e-invoicing into the product, with a 30-day free trial and 50,000+ zzp users. For Kees it is the clearest signal of where software-only competitors are heading: automated administration plus self-filed returns, without a human who carries the responsibility.

players.name: MoneyMonk
players.description: MoneyMonk is a Utrecht-based zzp accounting app built around time tracking, invoicing, receipts and VAT returns for freelancers, sold in a Starter tier that is free for 15 months for new registrations and Pro and Ultra tiers around EUR 32.50 to 37.50 per month, with strong review scores in the app stores and on Google. It competes with Kees for the same zzp audience, Utrecht included, on ease of use and a free first year, and is the typical tool a starter uses before deciding that filing and advice are worth paying for.

players.name: Rompslomp
players.description: Rompslomp, from Den Haag and part of Visma, is a lightweight zzp bookkeeping app that covers invoicing, VAT returns, receipts, e-invoicing and mobile apps for the freelancer who wants 'no hassle' rather than a full accounting suite, and carries 900+ reviews at 4.3 stars on Google and FeedbackCompany. Like SnelStart it belongs to Visma, but it is aimed at the micro-entrepreneur rather than the SME with an accountant, and competes with Kees for the same starters and creative freelancers who are price-sensitive and used to doing things on their phone.

players.name: SnelStart
players.description: SnelStart, founded in Alkmaar in 1982 and part of Visma, is one of the largest Dutch SME accounting suites: bookkeeping, invoicing, bank links and VAT returns for 165,000 entrepreneurs, sold both directly and through the accountants who work in the same file, with 215 employees, five offices, ISO 27001 certification and a 4.6 Trustpilot score. It is the package a growing VOF or BV client is likely to meet when an external accountancy firm proposes to take over the administration, and therefore the suite Kees and Founders must beat on the seamless path from starter to BV.

players.name: Traditional local bookkeepers and administratiekantoren (generic)
players.description: A generic entry for the thousands of local bookkeepers, administratiekantoren and small accountancy practices that still serve most Dutch freelancers and small businesses: the client delivers a shoebox, a folder or an export from an accounting package, the bookkeeper processes it periodically, files the VAT and income tax returns and charges by the hour or per return, with annual accounts and advice as separate line items. This is the incumbent Kees de Boekhouder was founded in 2009 to replace and the source of most 'switch from a previous bookkeeper' onboardings: personal and trusted, but with unpredictable bills, little real-time insight, paper-based capture and no app. It is described qualitatively only; there is no single company or official statistic behind the category.
